_README: Corrections applied to Pathoplexus metadata before it is used, and to the
live LAPIS query the dashboard makes. This file is the single source of
truth for both; nothing else may rewrite a submitter's declared value.
These are other laboratories' Restricted Use records. A correction here
does not amend the submission - only Pathoplexus can do that, at the
submitter's request. It is a local, declared, reversible override so the
published figures are not wrong while the revision is pending, and every
entry must carry the evidence for it and be reported upstream.
A correction stays only until upstream acts. Once the submitter revises
the record the override stops matching, apply_metadata_corrections.py
reports it as superseded, and the entry should be deleted in the same
Each correction is applied ONLY where the record still holds the value in
'published'. When the submitter revises it, the correction stops matching,
apply_metadata_corrections.py reports it as superseded, and the entry
should be deleted. That way a stale override can never outlive the error
it was written for, or quietly overwrite a corrected value.

evidence: sampleReceivedDate is 2026-07-25, exactly one year after the stated collection date: the sample would have been received a year before it was taken.
sequencingDate is 2026-11-05 and the record is tagged outbreak=Bdbv-2026.

The genome is identical, zero differences, to six 2026 outbreak genomes, and sits a median of 10 substitutions from the rest of the outbreak. A genuine July 2025 genome would be ancestral to the outbreak, not embedded in the middle of it.
It is the only pre-2026 collection date among the 2026 outbreak records.
corrections.effect_if_uncorrected: Stretches the sequencing-volume chart back a full year, compressing the outbreak into the right-hand third of the panel. Excluded from the rooting regression anyway by --min-year 2026.
